remaining_limitations: The tick does not yet allocate execution identity (start_execution is not called at spawn), so live local agents are legacy records and keep the pre-existing launch PID path; the namespace check applies once records carry execution_id and a local runtime target. The package that allocates execution identity must write process_namespace, pid and pid_start into a local runtime target at start, or refuse start_execution for a local record without them: a record with an execution_id and no local process identity is refused as runtime target names no process and can never be retired. The end to end test seeds that target by hand, so the spawn path is not covered.

HerdrRuntime.live_names, reported, conversations and reap_name still read this host's process table by agent name (through terminate_agent.sessions). The tick reap pass and the launch check no longer judge remote agents with them, but master recovery, take master, resume, lifetime, the stray sweep and the swarm CLI still call them; those callers handle local agents only today. The stray sweep reaps only local processes carrying a name this swarm issued and retired.

hooks.context.account_sessions counts live sessions per Claude account from this host's process table for quota placement; it is local by design and unchanged. scripts.terminate_agent stays the operator's local CLI, with its caller and process-group checks unchanged.

A remote agent with no answer stays suspect and keeps its claim lease indefinitely; nothing escalates it to the operator yet, and fencing a returning attempt against a replacement belongs to the generation fencing work (INV-R07). A remote backend without the observe capability reads as unknown, so its agents stay suspect rather than being judged lost.

unqualified_process_actions_rejected_total counts terminate refusals for missing or unqualified process identity only; unavailable backends and foreign backend refusals are counted elsewhere or not at all. It is an in-process counter on RuntimeRouter with no exporter.
No remote backend exists yet; the remote runtime is a fixture. No live rollout proof.
